One of the most well-known approaches is the greedy algorithm, which selects intervals based on their end points.

1. Sort the intervals by their end points.
2. Select the first interval from the sorted list.
3. For each subsequent interval, select it if it does not overlap with the previously selected interval.
This algorithm runs in $ O(n \log n) $ time due to the sorting step.
### 1.2.2 Dynamic Programming Approach
Another approach is to use dynamic programming. Let $ dp[i] $ be the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals that can be selected from the first $ i $ intervals. The recurrence relation is:
$$

This approach also runs in $ O(n^2) $ time.
